How to use

  • Add 3 drops to a bowl of steaming water and inhale under a towel.
  • Diffuse 4 drops alongside lemon and tea tree.
  • Dilute to 2% in carrier oil for a warming chest rub.

Dilute before applying to skin and patch-test first. Not for internal use.

Who it's for

The change of season

The oil most people buy once a year, when the weather turns and the house starts to feel closed up.

Steam inhalation

The classic use: a few drops in a bowl of hot water, a towel over the head, and a few minutes of breathing.

Post-exercise rubs

Common in chest and muscle blends at low dilution for the cooling, opening quality.

What people get wrong

Using too much in a steam bowl. Three drops is the right number. People use ten, find it overwhelming to the point of stinging, and conclude the oil is too strong rather than the dose.

Diffusing it around young children. Like peppermint, the 1,8-cineole that makes eucalyptus useful is the same compound that makes it unsuitable for babies and toddlers.

What it won't do

It is not a treatment for anything. It smells clearing and many people find steam comforting when they are congested, but the steam is doing most of that work and neither will shorten an illness.

We describe how our oils smell and how people use them. We don't make medical claims, because essential oils aren't medicine.

Questions about Eucalyptus Clearing

Which eucalyptus is this?

Eucalyptus globulus, the blue gum, which is the high-cineole type most people mean by eucalyptus. Eucalyptus radiata is gentler and E. citriodora smells of lemon — all three are sold simply as 'eucalyptus'.

Can I use it in the shower?

Yes. A few drops on the shower floor, away from where the water lands directly, will evaporate in the steam. Do not apply it to your skin in the shower, where hot water increases absorption.

Is it safe around children?

Not for babies and young children. Cineole-rich oils can affect breathing in the very young. For a household with small children, ask a doctor before diffusing it at all.

How long does it keep once opened?

Two to three years stored properly — cool, dark and tightly closed. Distilled oils keep considerably better than cold-pressed citrus.

What dilution should I use on skin?

Around 2% for the body — roughly 12 drops per 30 ml of carrier oil — and 1% for the face. Always patch-test before wider use, and never apply neat.

Can I take it internally?

No. None of our oils are food grade and none are sold for internal use. Essential oils are extremely concentrated, and advice to add them to water or food is not advice we endorse.

How quickly will it arrive?

Orders are dispatched from Delhi within two business days and usually arrive within a further three to five, depending on where you are. Shipping is free over ₹999.
